name: Cost of compliance

subjectOf.text: Governance reform delivered through non and deferred prosecution agreements is comparatively cheap for corporations because it adversely affects only a small number of board and management positions.
subjectOf.abstract: N/DPA-related governance re- form is relatively "cheap" for corporations because comparatively few board and management positions are adversely affected.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy Lacine, The Effect of Deferred and Non-Prosecution Agreements on Corporate Governance Evidence from 1993-20 (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2486570

subjectOf.text: What breaks the compliance incentive is the possibility that a suspension never ends, not uncertainty about how long it lasts; a mean-preserving spread in a finite duration weakly lowers the cost of compliance.
subjectOf.abstract: Should intelligent agents have legal rights? This Article sets that question aside and asks a smaller one that matters more in practice. An intelligent agent that earns a reputation record has something to lose.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Should an Intelligent Agent Have Legal Rights? (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7596939
scope_conditions: mean of the finite duration held fixed
